items.title: Hank Green did nothing wrong
items.summary:
Hank Green got “caught” using AI… and I genuinely don’t think he did anything wrong.

The whole controversy started because Hank said “I appreciate the pushback” in a video — a phrase people thought sounded suspiciously like ChatGPT.

That led to Hank explaining that while he doesn’t use AI to write his scripts, he DOES use it to help find research papers that he then reads himself.

And somehow, that turned into a much bigger debate about whether creators should be using AI at all.

I actually understand why people care. If you watch someone specifically for THEIR opinions, perspective, and commentary, you probably don’t want those things outsourced to an LLM.

But using AI as a better research tool or dumping your own messy thoughts into it and asking it to help organize them feels like a completely valid use-case to me.

I also think people need to give creators a little more grace here.

Creators are often working under a ton of pressure to constantly research, write, film, edit, p

items.title: 3 New Ways To Use ChatGPT Codex
items.summary:
Most people are barely scratching the surface of what the new Codex app can do.

It can now browse social media without an API, turn something you build into a live, shareable website, and let you control work running on your computer directly from your phone.

To try it for yourself, you can use Codex with both the free and paid plans, although free accounts have lower usage limits and some features have separate requirements. 

Download the ChatGPT desktop app with the link in the pinned comment and try one of these today.

And SAVE this video to reference later.

#Codex #ChatGPT #OpenAI #AITools #AIhacks
items.author: Matt Wolfe
items.transcript: Here are three new ways to use Codex that you probably didn't even know existed. First, you can use it to scan social media without an API. Usually, if you want your AI to look for specific social media posts, you have to [music] connect to the platform's API. But now, Codex can open a browser, click through websites, and search posts or topics right within the Codex app. Second, you can build a dashboard, game, or web app and publish it on the web without ever leaving the Codex platform. [music] Just send it to sites where you can preview it, make changes, and publish it as a shareable link. No [music] separate hosting required. And third, you can turn your phone into the ultimate Codex booster. Just connect your iPhone to the desktop app through the remote feature, start a voice session, and you can talk to both ChatGPT [music] work or Codex while it operates on your computer. Ask it to update your website, check on a task, run tests, or change direction all while you're away from your desk. So, check out the Codex app today and try one of these for yourself.

items.title: Did This AI Company Go Too Far...?
items.summary:
Friend 2.0 might be the weirdest AI product launch I’ve seen all year 😭

The AI necklace can now talk back to you, and somehow the ad they made for it raises even more questions than the product itself.

The founder has described Friend as a kind of “confidant, friend, God,” says the first 5,000 devices sold out, and now wants to sell 50,000 of these.

And there are clearly people who genuinely want this. One commenter on X even said AI makes a better counselor than therapy.

So… am I being old-fashioned, or is this where we’re actually headed?

#AI #aitech #ainews
items.author: Matt Wolfe
items.transcript: What the did I just watch? Friend, the company behind the AI necklace, just released Friend 2.0 that can now talk back to you. And this is the actual ad that they released for it. >> When was the first time you felt this way? >> [music] >> A few years ago. >> [music] >> Just feel like I should have an answer now. >> It's okay to be confused. >> [music] >> I don't think so. >> It's not bad to be gay. >> I genuinely can't tell whether their entire marketing strategy is intentionally rage bait or whether they actually watched this and thought, "Yeah, this is a good useful product that people need." The founder literally described Friend as some kind of confidant, friend, god. And he said the first version sold through its initial run of 5,000 devices, and now he wants to sell 50,000 of these. And look, I am not an AI hater. I use AI every day. It's helped me build tools and grow my business in a way that honestly would have not been possible 5 years ago. And one comment even admitted, "As someone currently trying therapy, I got to say AI makes a much better counselor." So, I don't know. Maybe I'm just being old-fashioned here, but let me know in the comments what you think. And follow for more videos about what's happening in AI and tech right now.
